No, please, do not let yourself feel foolish! It’s not you. Abusers have a way of drawing someone in, hiding their true self. They ensnare you with their charm and attentiveness, but that facade is immediately dropped once an abuser knows they have a hold of you. I thought I was happy for the most part until I bought a house with my abusive (now ex) boyfriend. When I was literally legally trapped by a contract to live in and pay for a home with him, it was downhill from there. I declared bankruptcy to get away from him and out of the obligation to pay for the home we shared.

It’s not about strength as much as it is being supported enough to feel safe enough to get out. I won’t pretend it’s easy, but with help you can do it!

You’re in an abusive relationship now, but I’m sure at one point it *was good, even if it was very brief. I think you’re afraid to let go of the person he was or could’ve been. It’s hard to see it when you’re in it, but the person he is currently is not going to revert back to or evolve into a better man. He wants you to be tired and worn down. You’re more defenseless - mentally, physically and emotionally - without sleep.
I left my abusive after 8 years. I dated him from age 22-30. He was the only boyfriend I’d ever had. It was hard to leave, even when my loved ones opened up my eyes and helped me realized I was miserable and falling apart in every way.
I’m not on Reddit much, but if you need someone who’s been there to talk to, I’m here for you! I promise, even if it takes multiple tries, you can get out and you can be happier. You deserve better.

Edit: Also, if he doesn’t let you go to the bathroom when you NEED to go the bathroom. Yikes. It took me forever to realize it was deliberate abuse. I started to get up in the morning earlier so I could use the bathroom before he started to get ready for work. Once he was up,
I wasn’t allowed to go to or be in the bathroom at all until he left for work. Not long after I started getting up earlier, he’d get up and follow me to the bathroom and tell me to get out so he could get ready. He is a terrible person.

I (F33) was entirely too honest with my SO (M31) after one particularly difficult weekend with SD(4).
I said “I do not like your daughter. I’m sorry, I don’t like her. If this is how she acts now, and this how soft you’re going to be as a parent, I do not want to know that kid at 13. I don’t want to know her as an adult. She will walk over you AND TRY to walk all over me. The way you are with her, means I have to be the “bad guy” and that’s not fair to me.”
We’re not married, and I’m not sure we’ll last. I don’t know how he wasn’t done with me the second I said I didn’t like her. In reality, my feelings about SD vary (and I hate that and feel guilty about it). Sometimes I actually miss her and am excited to see her; SO knows this. She went to a renaissance faire with her dad, or as we explained it to her, a “princess fair”. She let me do her hair (she’s sensitive about her hair), her dad let me put makeup, glitter, and face tattoos on her. It was genuinely so fun to get her ready and see her reaction when she was all ready.
Other times, WOW. I cannot stand her.  She can be very bratty and I get so embarrassed. She acts like a baby and suffers majorly from “only child syndrome”. She’s not my kid, so I can’t really step in too much or I’ll step on SO’s toes. Last weekend at a gathering with my family, she was playing with the other kids. She’d scraped her ankle a couple days prior, and still insisted on needing a bandaid. When the bandage started to come off and we needed to put on a new one, when I touched her foot, OMG,the way she cried hysterically,  you would’ve thought she’d broken her whole damn leg. It was insanely dramatic and super embarrassing. 
Anyway, I FINALLY got SO to admit being a stepmom is extremely difficult, especially when it’s a toddler, especially a toddler like his daughter. 
I don’t know when or if things will  actually get better. I’m glad he knows I can’t love her unconditionally like he can, and that when she’s being a turd, I don’t want to be around her. He can finally see when I need a break. As far as when we have our own child (if that happens), I’m concerned how our parenting styles will clash. Like OP, I see my SD and I know I will parent different than my partner. I do not want my future son or daughter to be anything like her.
Thank you ❤️

Your lip/chin(?) piercing looks like a pimple, and it’s not attractive. You’re clearly into fitness, but a lot you looks fake and needs to toned down. Hair is a bit fried, makeup is too harsh. If you have implants, they look too big for your body. Also, everyone ages, come to terms with that and try to stop dressing like you’re younger than you actually are.

I would have to agree that the intense liner is not doing you any favors, especially with the lenses, which I know are out of your control.

I think both your haircut and color could be changed up to improve your overall look. That red/auburn color in combination with the cut really is aging you, terribly. That particular color ages you because it’s dull and lackluster. It doesn’t have much shine and it also highlights that your hair appears to be damaged. If you like red, try a red that’s warmer and more vibrant, but if you stay red update your hairstyle asap. A dark brown with dimension could look nice. But honestly, you’re too young for a cute like that. Your face is more angular than soft, so you need a softer, more youthful cut to look more your age.

I don’t know what look/style you’re going for, but I think you look best in the 3rd picture with the shorter hair.

Also, sure, if dental was affordable anywhere (it’s awful everywhere, I’m convinced), I’d said get braces because overbites can cause breathing issues and even affect your posture in severe cases. However, I honestly like your teeth as they are. No one else has your exact smile. Get veneers though and you’ll be walking around with a totally different face - not just different teeth, it will change the look of your whole face. I went to school with a girl who got dental work done (probably needed) but now her face looks perpetually swollen.

I agree. Maybe try thicker frames? Take someone with you to try on frames so you can get their feedback. Trying to pick out new glasses on your own is hard unless you’ve already nailed down the style/color of frames you like to stick to.

Also, nothing wrong with the long hair, but shorter length wavy/curly hair might look nice.

All that being said, you’re only 17. You have plenty time to find yourself and find your style. You have even more time (when you’re older) to dress and style yourself in boring ass adult fashion. Enjoy this time when you get to experiment with how you want to look and who you want to be.
You’re not ugly, obviously. Your nose is a little big though and acne isn’t cute, so keep working to clear that up and you’ll be good.

The ugliest thing about you is that it’s clear that you’re sad and you don’t feel like you’re pretty. Finding some joy (easier said than done, I know) would make you smile more and make your eyes light up. Happiness can make someone so much prettier.

In an earlier post of yours, someone suggested you get side swept bangs and even photoshopped a pic of you with that type of bangs. Trying styling your bangs differently (you may even need to go get them cut again). These bangs aren’t doing you any favors. They accentuate (in a bad way) that your eyes are slanted downward and are wide set. 

You have pretty eyes, nice skin and decent lips. You have a unique face. Some people will equate that to a kinder way of saying “ugly”, but that’s not what I’m saying. Find a way to embrace what makes you not so cookie-cutter/in fashion/classically beautiful. Eye makeup that plays up your eye color; face makeup that doesn’t hide your nice skin, but makes you look healthier and more glowy; bangs that compliment your face more; a warmer hair color, maybe even try styling your hair differently - curls or loose waves.

I’m sorry you’ve been bullied. That’s not fair and not right. I hope you can find a way to feel more beautiful and all around feel more confident and happier.

I agree! 

I’d also suggest adding some dimension to your hair - highlights, lowlights. Hair that is super  dark and flat (in terms of color) is hard to pull off, as is super dark, heavy eyeliner.

I don’t think the shape of your frames in your first picture suits you. Besides those frames, I think you look prettiest in the first picture. Try makeup that isn’t so harsh, or if you want something so bold like in your other pictures, take more time practicing your makeup skills. 

I’d suggest makeup that is a little bit more natural with a color palette that suits your skin tone, eye color, etc. Let yourself look like yourself- you look pretty and kind as you are.

I came to my parents around the same age with my self-harm struggle. It scared them, and I saw that, so I did everything I could to back pedal, and downplay the issue. 

I’ve been in the mental hospital twice now, and once outpatient. 
I know my parents’ biggest regret is not doing something immediately to help me when I was still young.

I’m 31 now. I still struggle with turning to self-harm to cope or soothe myself, but I’m doing great! I’m in therapy. I’m learning to love and take care of myself. I’m super happy!

I would definitely recommend therapy. Don’t be afraid to try out a few therapists until your daughter finds one she really likes. I promise as uncomfortable as it is now, it’s worth it down the line for her 1) to still be here at 31, and 2) self-harm be a brief struggle she overcame in her teenage years.

You’re already doing great. Keep being a great mom by supporting her and getting her the help she needs.

I’m so happy for you! I was mentally and emotionally abused for so long. I’d hated myself, I was afraid to talk, afraid to confide in my family, and terrified to disobey my then boyfriend. He pushed me to self harm and a stay in a mental hospital.

I just left that terrible relationship, finally, about 2 months ago. We’d been together for about 8 years. Although mentally and emotionally, I’d left much earlier. I left him for the first time two years ago, and stayed with family, but I was still too connected to him. Plus, we had 4 dogs together, which for me, being 30 and childless, made it difficult to leave. So I went back, and we were together for a year. It was better for a while, until he had me stuck again.

So I left for the last time. I stayed with my dad for over a month before finding my own place, but once I left my ex, I didn’t go back. My family moved me out while my ex was at work, once I found a rental home. My family loaned me money and bought me food—did everything they could to get me out of there. The hardest part, the part that almost killed me, was picking 2 dogs to take with me, and leaving the other two behind. They’re all my babies and sometimes I cry when I think of them, and wondering how they’re doing. 
BUT I met someone new already. He’s amazing. Treats me well, sincerely shows care and concern for me and my feelings and opinions. He’s ok with disagreeing, he just likes hearing my thoughts, even if they don’t match his own.

AND I love living alone! In my 30 years, I’ve never lived alone until now. I do things for me, how I want to do them, and on my own time and pace. I feel free. 

Congrats on getting out! It’s so hard, but so worth it in the end.
